messages.subject: Result interpretation
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nick,

I was hoping you could clarify my doubts regarding interpretation of the following DIVALIKE+J result (figure attached)  :

When you go from range A to B or A to C or A to D, it represents a founder event, since a dispersal event is anagenetic and would consist of the retention of the ancestral area (e.g. A to AB). Am I on the right track?

Thanks,

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Result interpretation
messages.body_plain:
Hi!  Yep, that's the basic interpretation, since you estimated j > 0.

Always look at the pie charts also, and for more complex cases, you have to keep in mind some other points when interpreting these plots:

http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears-mistakes-to-avoid#Most_prob_states_not_joint
======================
Ancestral range estimation, not ancestral area reconstruction
The plot of most-probable states is not the same thing as the best joint history
How do I get the best joint history
The plot of most-probable states is not the same thing as an estimate of event counts
======================

Cheers!
Nick

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] example plot
messages.body_plain:
Hi -- by default the script starts a PDF with the pdf() command.  After that, all graphics go into the PDF instead of to the screen.

You won't see it until dev.off() closes PDF writing, and the system() command opens the PDF file to the screen.  (It's conceivable that on some operating systems, you will have to go double-click on the pdf to open it.

If you want the graphic to open in an R window, comment out the pdf() line.
Cheers,
Nick

messages.subject: odd stochastic map result- identical maps
messages.subject_clean: odd stochastic map result- identical maps
messages.body_plain:
Dear Nick,

Thank you again for all of your help.

I would like to have 100 independent stochastic maps. However this is very memory intensive, so my strategy is to do several rounds of ~20 maps at a time, since they are supposed to be independent. However I am getting this odd result. Every group of 20 is identical to the previous group, when they should be stochastic. I mean that map 1 from the first round is equal to map 1 of the second round, and so on for map 2...map 20. Right now I have runInputsSlow = TRUE and runBSMslow = TRUE which I interpreted to mean that it re-estimates relevant parameters each time instead of loading previous results. So I am not sure how to change the code to get what I am looking for.

Best,
Liz

messages.subject: Total ML: output from optimx vs. stored in results file
messages.subject_clean: Total ML: output from optimx vs. stored in results file
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have a question regarding the (log) total Maximum Likelihood value of a BioGeoBEARS estimation: I used to retrieve it from the model output as saved to a .Rdata file, such as "res$total_loglikelihood" (-407 in my case). Now I realised, for a time-stratified analysis, that this value is not the same as the one one reported on screen at the end of the estimation (-380, = the value reported from optimx, column "value"). Am I right in assuming that these should be the same and correspond to the total log-likelihood? In that case, how come in my case they are different? Or do they refer to different things? Might it be a convergence issue (but the optimx output reports successful convergence)?

I based my model comparison by AIC on the values obtained from $total_loglikelihood for each model so far, but now I am a bit confused... Can anyone help me?

Thanks – Jan
